value.body: Relationship managers look after a set of customers for a bank, NBFC or wealth firm, handling their accounts, loans, deposits and investment products. The day is spent meeting or calling customers, resolving service issues, opening accounts and meeting product targets.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Com, BBA or an MBA; some banks hire graduates from any stream

items.label: Segments
items.value: Retail, priority / wealth, SME and corporate banking

items.label: Common credentials
items.value: NISM or IRDAI certifications for selling mutual funds or insurance

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join through bank campus drives, bank-run certificate or PO-style programmes, or as sales officers and branch associates who move into relationship roles. Selling mutual funds or insurance needs the relevant NISM or IRDAI certification, which employers often sponsor.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Explaining banking, loan and investment products in plain terms
Managing a customer portfolio and follow-ups
Using the bank's CRM and core banking system

value.title: At a glance
items: Most roles are target-driven; incentives are part of pay.
Common next steps: senior RM, wealth or priority banking, branch manager, or credit roles.
Retail and SME roles involve a lot of fieldwork and customer visits.
